As each node is visited, briefly glow it and append its value to a horizontal output list at the bottom of the screen in left-to-right order.

manual: Instructions for the Experiment: Binary Tree Level-order Traversal DemonstrationI. Basic Experiment InformationExperiment Title: Binary Tree Level-order Traversal DemonstrationSubject: Engineering - Computer ScienceObjective: To visually demonstrate level-order (breadth-first) traversal of a binary tree and understand how nodes are visited level by level from top to bottom and left to right.II. Experimental Materials and EnvironmentA simple binary tree diagram with 7 nodes labeled 1–7; light-colored background; animation or visualization tool capable of highlighting nodes and displaying an output list.III. Experimental Procedure1. Preparation: Display a simple complete binary tree with node 1 as the root, nodes 2 and 3 as its children, and nodes 4–7 as the third level, all on a light background.2. Initialization: Prepare an empty horizontal output list at the bottom of the screen.3. Core Operation: Begin level-order traversal.   a. Highlight the root node (1) in a bright color such as red; briefly apply a glow effect.   b. Append value 1 to the output list.   c. Move to the next level and highlight nodes 2 and 3 from left to right, one by one, each with a brief glow, appending their values in order.   d. Proceed to the third level and highlight nodes 4, 5, 6, and 7 from left to right, appending each value to the output list as it is visited.4. Completion: Stop the traversal when all nodes have been visited and the output list contains 1–7 in level-order.IV. Observation of Experimental Phenomena1. Initial State: All nodes are visible but unhighlighted; output list is empty.2. During Traversal: Nodes are highlighted level by level from top to bottom; within each level, nodes are highlighted from left to right; each highlight is followed by an update to the output list.3. Final State: All nodes have been highlighted once; the output list shows a complete left-to-right sequence: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.V. Summary of Experimental PrincipleLevel-order traversal, also known as breadth-first traversal, visits nodes of a binary tree level by level starting from the root. It uses the principle of visiting all nodes at a given depth before moving to the next depth, typically implemented with a queue. The visualization demonstrates this principle by sequentially highlighting nodes by level and appending their values to an output list in the exact visiting order.
high_level_evaluation_guide: Target concept: Binary tree level-order (breadth-first) traversal. Minimum assumptions: a static binary tree structure with fixed node positions and labels, and a visualization system capable of sequential highlighting and list updates. Expected phenomena storyline: Phase 1 shows the full tree and empty output list; Phase 2 highlights the root and appends its value; Phase 3 highlights second-level nodes left to right with corresponding output updates; Phase 4 highlights third-level nodes left to right, completing the output list. Key causal transitions: node highlight represents a visit, which directly causes the node value to appear in the output list. Visibility constraints: the entire tree and the output list must remain visible throughout to verify order and correctness.
